sections.content:
24,635 people

were counted on the census as "finance officers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Finance officers oversee book-keeping, general accounting and other financial and related clerical functions mainly within local government and a variety of public sector organisations.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "finance officers", 15.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "finance officers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "finance officers" included:

  • printers
  • health and safety managers and officers
  • public services associate professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "finance officers" there were more women than men (75.7% compared with 24.3%).

This means "finance officers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 24.3% and women made up 75.7% of "finance officers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "finance officers" included:

  • podiatrists
  • careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists
  • credit controllers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "finance officers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "finance officers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "finance officers", 10.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (68.7% compared with 31.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.6%) than self-employed (1.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
